title: Pipelines
overview_description: Pipelines let you transform and process messages coming from streams. Pipelines consist of stages where rules are evaluated and applied. Messages can go through one or more stages.
pipeline_details_description:
Pipelines let you transform and process messages coming from streams. Pipelines consist of stages where rules are evaluated and applied. Messages can go through one or more stages.
After each stage is completed, you can decide if messages matching all or one of the rules continue to the next stage.
rules_page_description: Rules are a way of applying changes to messages. A rule consists of a condition and a list of actions. The condition is evaluated against a message, and the actions are executed if the condition is satisfied.

debug_metrics.banner_text: Debug metrics add overhead to message processing and increase memory usage. Disable them when you are finished troubleshooting. Pipeline Load values are smoothed over a 15-minute window and may take a few minutes to stabilize after enabling.
debug_metrics.help: Pipeline Load (15m) shows the relative share of pipeline rule execution time across the cluster. Enable debug metrics to start collecting timer data. Values may take up to about 15 minutes to populate after enabling, and collection adds overhead to message processing.

metrics_config.warning: Rule metrics should only be enabled to debug a performance issue because collecting the metrics will slow down message processing and increase memory usage.
metrics_config.pipeline_load_info: Enabling these metrics will add a new column to the Pipeline and Pipeline Rule pages called <columnName>Pipeline Load</columnName>, which will contain % values showing relatively, which of your Pipelines is consuming the most thread time.
metrics_config.rule_load_info: Enabling these metrics will also add a new column to the Pipeline Detail page called <columnName>Rule Load</columnName>, This will identify which Pipeline rules within the selected Pipeline are the most expensive.
